messages:
joan: Quick design pass request — exploring a darker baseline for Console v2. Main goals: keep syntax readable at 12px monospace, make charts pop without adding vibrance, and hit WCAG AA for UI text. Thoughts on the palette below?

joan: proposed colors (rough):
- --bg-900: #0b0c0f (baseline background)
- --bg-800: #111217 (panel background)
- --surface-600: #16171b (cards)
- --muted-300: #9aa0a6 (secondary text)
- --primary-400: #57b6ff (accent)
- --accent-warm: #ffb86b (warning-ish accent for charts)

joan: immediate nit — axis labels on the time-series are getting lost. 1px gridlines with current --muted-300 are barely visible on screenshots.

mike: agree. Can we try `--axis-line: rgba(255,255,255,0.06)` and `--gridline: rgba(255,255,255,0.03)`? Works better for dark backgrounds without making charts look too bright. :eyes:

shreya: quick contrast check: body text `#d7dbe0` on `#0b0c0f` = ~6.9:1 so fine. But muted labels at `#9aa0a6` drop to ~3.6:1 — not AA for normal text. We should reserve muted for microcopy only.

camila: for syntax highlighting: total avoidance of saturated greens/blues that clash with token heatmaps. Proposal: soften keywords to `#82cfff`, strings `#ffc88b`, functions `#d0a6ff`, types `#b9f6d6`. Keep contrasts >4.5 where possible at 12px.

joan: good call. Also for charts: instead of heavy saturation, use layered tones — e.g., primary series `#57b6ff`, secondary `#3a8fd6` (desaturated), tertiary `#7aa6d9` (lighter). For alerts use `--accent-warm` but with 0.12 alpha overlays for fills.

mike: small CSS snippet I tried in the prototype:```css
:root{
  --bg-900:#0b0c0f;
  --text:#d7dbe0;
  --muted-300:#9aa0a6;
  --primary-400:#57b6ff;
  --axis-line:rgba(255,255,255,0.06);
}
.chart .line{stroke:var(--primary-400);stroke-width:2}
```

shreya: accessibility nit — hover/focus states need 3:1 contrast against the immediate background per WCAG 2.2 for UI components. Buttons and toggles currently rely on outline alone; let's add subtle background tints for focus.

camila: color-blind friendly check: with the palette above, deuteranopia simulation still distinguishes series if we keep luminance differences. I'll run the sim and post screenshots.

design-bot: Deploy preview available: https://preview.redwood.design/coalshift-223 (build 382).

joan: thanks — small copy tweak: change "Latency" axis label to "P95 latency (ms)" in the default view, makes it clearer for folks scanning.

mike: layout thought — consider a toggle in top-right to switch between "Contrast: Default / High" that flips `--muted-300` to `#c6cad0` and increases gridline alpha. Useful for accessibility mode.

shreya: +1. Also add an a11y test to storybook that checks color tokens for 3:1 and 4.5:1 depending on token role.

camila: posted two screenshots in #design-to-dev with deuteranopia sim and axis tweaks. Link: https://img.redwood/company/coalshift-sims.png

aiden: quick implementation note from infra side — keep an eye on streaming charts: adding alpha overlays can increase overdraw on webgl canvas. prefer baked colors for lines and use fills sparingly.

joan: great — next steps: camila runs color-blind sim and posts variants, mike wires the toggle prototype, shreya adds the Storybook test, aiden checks perf impact. I'll collect results and schedule a 15-min sync tomorrow. :calendar:

mike: sounds good. I'll push a branch with the `--contrast-mode` variables and a tiny toggle control.

shreya: I'll write the test and add steps to the PR template for contrast checks.

camila: uploading alternative swatches now. :paintbrush:

joan: thanks team. If anybody sees any odd combinations in their apps, ping me directly — especially any chart legend collisions when the user has small displays.

mike: noted — will test on 13" laptop. :macbook:

(reacts: :thumbsup: from camila, :rocket: from aiden)
